name: Ethyl nicotinate
description: Ethyl nicotinate (CAS 614-18-6 ), also known commercially as Ignicut, is the ethyl ester of nicotinic acid used as a pharmaceutical intermediate, flavoring agent, and functional ingredient across multiple industries. It serves as a building block in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients and as a precursor in catalyst systems. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a key intermediate in the synthesis of niacin derivatives. Other nicotinic acid-based APIs utilize this compound where ester reactivity drives efficient conversion pathways. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into topical products targeting skin circulation effects, particularly in warming formulations. As a flavoring agent, it contributes to tobacco and food flavor profiles where pyridine-type notes are required. It carries a recognized FEMA status supporting its use in regulated flavor applications worldwide. In catalyst development, it acts as a ligand precursor or coordination compound in heterogeneous and homogeneous catalytic systems. The material is available as a colorless to pale yellow liquid in standard commercial packaging. It is supplied in pharmaceutical-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the purity requirements of API synthesis.
